News.title: Two arrested after probe into lawyers ‘who told illegal migrants to pose as GAY & say wives are lesbians to get asylum’
News.content:
MIGRANT PROBE Two arrested after probe into lawyers ‘who told illegal migrants to pose as GAY & say wives are lesbians to get asylum’

TWO people have been arrested after a probe was launched into lawyers who told migrants to pose as gay to help their asylum claims.

Coordinated raids were carried out in east London by the Home Office after an investigation was launched in response to the allegations.



A woman in her late forties was arrested on suspicion of providing an immigration service contrary to section 91 of the Immigration and Asylum Act.



And a man in his early twenties was arrested on suspicion of fraud, a Home Office source said.

Immigration Minister Mike Tapp said: “If lawyers, or so-called lawyers, and legal advisers are out there providing this dodgy advice, we’re coming after that. And as you’ve seen today, we’ll make those arrests.

“Our asylum system is there for people who are genuinely fleeing persecution and war and I’m really proud of that. But people that are trying to abuse it will not be accepted.”

It comes after a BBC undercover investigation revealed how migrants whose visas are due to expire are being instructed how to obtain fake evidence, including supporting letters and photographs, to support asylum claims.

The investigation secretly filmed at an event for LGBT asylum seekers with attendees telling an undercover reporter that most of them were not genuinely gay.

After the shocking revelations the Home Office announced an investigation in response.

News.title: Shocking moment two thugs lob 240-litre wheelie bin over bridge and onto police car leaving officer in hospital
News.content:
THIS is the terrifying moment a pair of thugs toss a 240-litre wheelie bin off a bridge onto a police car travelling beneath them at 60-mph.

Shocking footage shows the bin being hurled from a footbridge before smashing through the windscreen of the marked patrol car as it passes below.





PC Lydia Cope was left bloodied after suffering cuts to her hands and an eye injury when the heavy bin crashed onto the vehicle and caved in the windscreen.

She had been on a routine patrol along the A442 near Telford, Shropshire, with colleague PC Alex Morton-Nash at around 1.52am.

The car was not using blue lights or sirens at the time.

Despite her injuries and the shattered windscreen, PC Cope managed to keep control and safely pull over.



Both officers were taken to the hospital for treatment but returned to work the following day.

Daniel Hodnett, 20, and a 17-year-old accomplice had stolen the bin from Hoop Mill in Hadley, a court heard.

The pair then dragged it to a footbridge over the Wombridge Interchange.

They then lay in wait for a passing vehicle before launching the bin onto the road below.

The pair fled the scene but were later identified through a social media appeal and arrested days later.



In March Hodnett, of Clock Tower Avenue, Wrockwardine Wood, and the teenager admitted a string of offences.

He admitted causing criminal damage recklessly endangering life, causing danger to road users, theft and further criminal damage charges.

This week, at Telford Magistrates’ Court, Hodnett was handed a two-year suspended sentence.

Hodnett was also ordered to complete 150 hours of unpaid work.

The 17-year-old, who cannot be named for legal reasons, was referred to the Youth Offending Team.



Superintendent Edward Hancox said: “The actions of Hodnett and his accomplice were nothing short of reckless and irresponsible, and I have no doubt in my mind they could have caused serious harm to road users that night.

“It is pure luck that PC Cope and PC Morton-Nash suffered only minor injuries as it could have had a much worse outcome.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Thanks to PC Cope’s calmness she was able to pull the vehicle to a safe stop, preventing further harm to any other road users.

“I hope today’s sentence sends a strong message that this behaviour will not be tolerated.”

News.title: Inside ‘House of Horrors’ where evil beast tortured women in sick dungeon with blood-stained walls and clumps of hair
News.content:
VINCENT Agar has been on the run for a quarter of a century after he fled the UK in the wake of his despicable crimes.

The 80-year-old subjected his victims to a series of terrifying ordeals after kidnapping them and holding them hostage in his house of horrors.





Chilling pictures have now revealed the grim interior of the home where the drug-fuelled beast kept two women prisoner and tortured them in his cellar.

This week, he was jailed for 19 years, and police have now released horrifying photos of his dingy flat in Middlesbrough, where he carried out his warped crimes.

Photos show blood stains on the walls and what appear to be clumps of hair on the floor of his flat in Parliament Road.

Agar even installed a “trap door” which he could lock to prevent the women from escaping his grim dungeon.

One victim told how he threatened to shoot her after she saw a girl tied to a radiator.

Agar, who was extradited from his bolthole in Thailand last year, was jailed at Durham Crown Court this week.

He was found guilty of six charges, including grievous bodily harm, false imprisonment, threats to kill and drug dealing.

Judge Richard Bennett branded Agar “a violent and sadistic bully” telling him: “Your offending has now caught up with you.





“You revelled in holding power over some of the most vulnerable women in our society.

“Your flat was like a fortress. You had installed a number of doors to the interior to prevent access. They also prevented escape.

“I reject your evidence that these doors were installed for either draft exclusion or because you were being burgled.

“These were classic security measures of a drug dealer designed to prevent the police getting into your flat before you could dispose of drugs.

“That anti-police security also created a barrier which prevented [first victim] from escaping.

“You got away with committing these serious offences for 25 years, and this has now caught up on you.”



The court heard Agar tortured the women between 1998 and 2000 when he was a drug dealer.

One of the women told how Agar cut her with hot knives, burned her with an iron and a crackpipe gauze.

On another occasion, he beat her so hard with a metal hoover pole that it broke.

He also threatened to break her fingers with a wrench, punched her, poured hot kettle water over her and cut off her hair and burned her with cigarettes.

During another ordeal, Agar kept the woman prisoner for three days while carrying out a series of vile crimes.

She told how she saw a “torture chamber” in his flat which included a wooden chair which were fitted with ankle and wrist straps.

The second victim was detained in Agar’s flat and threatened with a gun after she saw a “scared” girl tied to a radiator.

Agar installed three doors which he used as an “elaborate security arrangement” to dispense his “own sort of justice”.



Agar fled the UK in 2000, where he evaded justice for a quarter of a century.

Detectives at Cleveland Police began investigating Agar’s sick crimes in 2019 before he was finally brought to justice.

Agar had been living in Koh Samui, Thailand, before he was arrested and extradited to face the charges.

Sophie Johnston, defending, said Agar’s addiction to crack cocaine was “his downfall”.

Agar showed no reaction as he was jailed.

News.title: War comes to Putin’s door as ship goes up in flames in sight of £1bn palace where paranoid tyrant is ‘hiding in bunker’
News.content:
This is the moment the war finally arrived at the front gates of Vladimir Putin’s £1 billion clifftop mega-mansion.

Thick black smoke was seen billowing from a stricken vessel right off the coast of Gelendzhik.





The burning hulk is suspected to be a “shadow fleet” tanker used by Putin to dodge international oil sanctions.

The inferno broke out in full view of the tyrant’s palace, which is famously kitted out with high-tech underground bunkers.

Putin is said to be hiding out in his bolt-hole, terrified of a Ukrainian drone strike or a coup from his own inner circle.

The Russian tyrant is under fire at home as his “endless war” strategy continues to drain Russia dry.



The blazing ship was spotted just ten miles from his doorstep – well within eyesight of the dictator’s terrace.

Details of the “inferno vessel” are being kept under wraps by tight-lipped Russian officials.



But news of the blaze follows urgent alerts from monitoring groups over a fresh wave of Ukrainian aerial and marine drones.

In a typical show of defiance, Putin snubbed an olive branch ceasefire proposal from Volodymyr Zelensky that was set to start at midnight.

Instead, he offered a measly two-day truce on Friday and Saturday only.



His forces then launched a brutal blitz on Kharkiv and Zelensky’s home city of Kryvyi Rih early on Wednesday morning.

One civilian was killed in a Russian drone strike on the border region of Sumy.

Shockingly, many of these deadly attacks rained down just six hours after the “silence” regime was supposed to begin.



Kyiv has now warned that if Russia won’t play ball with the ceasefire, Moscow could be in the crosshairs this weekend.

Ukraine could target Putin’s prized Victory Day military parade on Saturday as thousands of troops gather in the Red Square.

The Kremlin boss is set to give a tub-thumping speech amid a massive security ring-fencing of the Russian capital.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha blasted the move, saying it proves Putin has zero interest in real diplomacy.

Sybiha said: “Putin is only concerned with military parades, not human lives.”



Defiant Kyiv chiefs warned that since Russia rejected the May 6 truce, the Ukrainian military won’t be holding back on May 9.

Russia has hit back with chilling threats of nuclear-scale strikes on Kyiv if their parade is interrupted by drones.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The latest carnage follows a savage Russian assault that killed 25 people in a single day – the bloodiest of the year so far.

But Ukraine isn’t taking it lying down, reportedly smashing a Russian FSB command post in occupied Crimea with a flurry of drones.

News.title: Monster jailed for murdering top chef who was found dead in blood-stained sleeping bag in derelict building
News.content:
LOCKED UP Monster jailed for murdering top chef who was found dead in blood-stained sleeping bag in derelict building

A THUG has been jailed for murdering a top London chef who was found in a blood-stained sleeping bag in a derelict building.

Alexis De Naray, 45, trained at the Prue Leith Cooking School and worked in several high-end kitchens including Claridge’s.





But he began drinking due to the “stressful nature of the job” and later became a chronic alcoholic and homeless.

Alexis’ body was discovered last June in the attic room of an abandoned building in Shrewsbury, Shropshire.

He had suffered 17 fractured ribs and and a brain haemorrhage, which showed signs of significant blunt force trauma before his death.

Adam Rowson, 26, was today jailed for life with a minimum of 16 years after he was found guilty of murdering Alexis following a trial.

In a victim impact statement Alexis’ father, a former shipping and oil executive, said his death had a “devastating” effect on the family.

“Alexis, my wonderful boy, did not deserve to lose his life prematurely and in such a violent way,” he added.



“He was a dear son who will shall be forever missed. Losing him has had a life-changing effect on us as a family.

“Everyone who knew Alexis loved him.

“He was a very talented chef and worked for many years in London until he became unwell.

“He was gradually getting better when he sadly and unexpectedly lost his life.

“We are devastated at having lost him. No parent should have to bury their child.



“Alexis will be missed very much.”

Stafford Crown Court heard Alexis was a “well-educated man” from a Greek family.

Sally Howes KC, prosecuting, said: “Having attended the Prue Leith Cooking School, he worked as a head chef in a number of restaurants in London.

“Unfortunately, due to the stressful nature of that job, drinking became a way of life and his alcohol problems began.

“By the time of his death he had become a chronic alcoholic.”



Jurors were told Alexis met Rowson at the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital and the pair were seen on CCTV shortly before 4am the next morning walking towards the derelict building.

Once inside, the chef was brutally attacked before Rowson used the victim’s bank card to buy alcohol and scratchcards.

His body was eventually discovered under a bloodied sleeping bag in an attic room of the derelict property.

Alexis had suffered 17 fractured ribs and a brain haemorrhage, which showed signs of significant blunt force trauma.

A post mortem revealed he had near-fatal levels of alcohol in his system.



Detective Inspector Joanne Delahay, who led the investigation, said: “Alexis died as a result of a vicious and prolonged assault at the hands of Rowson.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I’m pleased that he has been found guilty today and will now face a substantial amount of time in prison.

“Our thoughts remain with Alexis’s family and friends, who have been incredibly strong throughout this ordeal.”

News.title: Mum-of-two ‘stabbed to death by “angry” partner who then tried to kill himself by triggering gas blast at family home’
News.content:
BLAST 'MURDER' Mum-of-two ‘stabbed to death by “angry” partner who then tried to kill himself by triggering gas blast at family home’

A MUM-of-two was stabbed to death by her “angry” partner who then tried to kill himself by triggering a gas blast, a court heard.

Clifton George is accused of murdering Annabel Rook, 46, during a row at their home in Stoke Newington, North London, on June 17, 2025.





Jurors heard Annabel had told George, 45, to leave as their relationship began to fall apart.

He allegedly took a knife from the kitchen and stabbed the judge’s daughter to death before hatching a plan to kill himself and “explode the house”.

Snaresbrook Crown Court heard he started a fire in the home by setting a gas cannister alight in the basement and triggering “an enormous explosion”.

The blast caused significant damage to the property – including lifting the floorboards and moving furniture.



Neighbours were woken by a “massive boom which felt like a mini-earthquake”, it was said.

George was found in the back garden “bleeding heavily and trying to stab himself with a shard of broken glass”, jurors were told.



He said his wife was inside the house but told emergency crews he knew she was dead.

When asked how he knew she was dead, he replied: “Because I killed her.”

Annabel, who was the co-founder of a London-based social enterprise called MamaSuze, was found inside with “many” stab wounds.

Prosecutor William Emlyn Jones KC said: “On the night of June 16 and 17 last year, the defendant argued with his partner Annabel Rook.

“In the course of that argument he punched her, he then tried to strangle her, and then he went to the kitchen to get a knife, he came back with the knife and he stabbed her to death.



“He was undoubtedly very angry with her, and we will be at looking at why he was so angry.”

In a police interview, George said he “lost it” when he found out Annabel had “lied to me”, jurors were told.

The court heard the couple never married but had been living together for just over a decade.

Mr Emlyn Jones said: “In the summer of 2025 it had broken down to the extent that they were heading towards a break-up.

“Annabel had told the defendant that he had to leave.



“The evidence of their relationship in the last few years of Annabel’s life will come in the form of evidence from her family, and from their friends, but also from messages and notes recovered from their telephones, which provide an accurate and contemporaneous record of what was going on as their relationship deteriorated, and how they both felt about it.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

George has admitted responsibility for Annabel’s death by pleading guilty to manslaughter but he denies murder.

The trial continues.

News.title: First look inside rat virus cruise quarantined in Atlantic with deserted decks & guests in masks after hazmat docs board
News.content:
EERIE footage from inside a rat-infested cruise liner has revealed ghostly empty decks and masked passengers – as hazmat teams boarded the stricken vessel.

Nearly 150 people remain trapped on the Dutch ship MV Hondius off the coast of Cape Verde, with most confined to their cabins as panic spreads onboard.





Three passengers are dead and at least four more are sick.

The luxury liner has been left stranded at the Port of Praia after local authorities refused to let it dock “with the aim of protecting national public health”.

Now the floating hotspot is heading towards Spain – despite a furious warning from Canary Islands leader Fernando Clavijo.

He said he “cannot allow” the virus-hit vessel into his territory as it edges closer to Europe.



Chilling video, obtained by AP, shows near-deserted decks, with only a handful of figures in medical masks wandering the ship.

Inside, the once-bustling interior lounges and dining halls have fallen into an unsettling hush as people follow strict COVID-like quarantine rules.



Ship operator Oceanwide Expeditions said it had implemented its highest level of response, with isolation measures, hygiene protocols and medical monitoring.

Fears are mounting that passengers who shared a flight with an infected woman could become super spreaders.

Health officials are scrambling to trace contacts after the woman disembarked on one of the world’s most remote islands.



The virus is not usually passed between people – but experts are divided.

The World Health Organisation (WHO) warned that the disease may have spread between passengers aboard the luxury cruise.

Clavijo warned he did not have enough information “to reassure the public or guarantee their safety” if the ship docks in the Canaries.



But Spain’s Health Ministry has signalled it will take the vessel in.

Officials said the ship would be received “in accordance with international law and humanitarian principles”.

The MV Hondius is expected to reach Santa Cruz de Tenerife within days.

Three deaths linked to hantavirus have already sparked global alarm.



A government statement said the islands were the “closest location with the necessary capabilities” to treat those onboard.

It added: “Spain has a moral and legal obligation to assist these people, among whom are also several Spanish citizens.”

Meanwhile, a British man is fighting for his life in intensive care in South Africa.

An unwell British crew member – believed to be the ship’s doctor – and a Dutch patient are still suffering “acute respiratory symptoms” and need urgent treatment.



On Monday, WHO confirmed seven cases of hantavirus onboard.

That includes three deaths, one critically ill patient and three with milder symptoms.

One hantavirus patient who was a passenger on the MV Hondius is now being treated in Zurich, Switzerland.



As well as the Swiss case, three passengers, two with acute symptoms, are being evacuated from the MV Hondius to the Netherlands via airlift.

One is the British crew member, a German passenger and another crew member from the Netherlands.

Oceanwide Expeditions said two of the passengers to be flown off the ship by specialist aircraft were suffering symptoms, and a third was “closely associated” with the passenger who died on May 2.

“A definitive disembarkation point for the remaining guests on board has not been finalised,” they added.

That leaves 149 people from 23 countries stranded at sea – waiting for answers.



Evacuation plans for other guests remain in chaos.

“We’re working with Spanish authorities who… have said that they will welcome the ship to do a full investigation, a full epidemiologic investigation, full disinfection of the ship and of course, to assess the risk of the passengers that are actually on board,” said Maria Van Kerkhove.

But Spain quickly pushed back – insisting “no decision” had yet been made.

Hantaviruses are spread by rodents – through urine, droppings and saliva.



What Is Hantavirus HANTAVIRUS is one of the deadliest diseases for humans, comparable to Ebola. It is a rare pathogen primarily carried by rodents but can also be transmitted to humans via droppings and urine. The virus can lead to serious illnesses, including hantavirus pulmonary syndrome (HPS) and haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS). Each hantavirus strain is associated with a specific rodent species and is transmitted to humans through exposure to infected rodents’ urine, feces, or saliva, and less commonly through rodent bites. The virus was first identified during the 1950s Korean War near the Hantan River and is not easily spread between humans. Despite its rarity, hantavirus has a high mortality rate of 38 percent, based on CDC data. There is no specific treatment or cure. Symptoms of hantavirus infection include fever, kidney damage, fatigue, vomiting, and reddish cheeks, with an incubation period ranging from four days to two months. Humans are at risk of infection through contact with wild or pet rodents, their droppings, or through the mucous membranes of the eyes, nose, or mouth. To date, no confirmed cases of direct human-to-human transmission of hantavirus have been reported.

They can cause anything from flu-like illness to deadly respiratory or haemorrhagic disease.

According to UK Government hantavirus advice, symptoms usually appear two to four weeks after exposure, although they can develop much faster – from as little as two days – or take as long as eight weeks.

That means further cases could still emerge among passengers in the coming days and weeks, as the infection window remains wide open.

Early signs include fatigue, fever, muscle pain and severe headaches.

Clavijo warned: “This decision is not based on any technical criteria, ⁠nor is there sufficient ⁠information to reassure ⁠the public or guarantee their safety.”



Passengers and crew will undergo medical checks before being flown home.

Canary Islands spokesman Alfonso Cabello told Telecinco: “We can’t understand why there’s been a change in the strategy that had been adopted without us being told.

“If the situation on the ship is one of relative calm which appears to be the case, why are passengers and crew going to be subjected to three of four more days at sea so they can reach the Canary Islands.

“Why not evacuate them directly via the international airport in Cape Verde?

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are talking about a virus that, according to the specialists we have heard, seems to pose no risk between humans but other specialists are not saying the same. We do not exactly know what strain it is, whether it has mutated or not.



“I believe that this lack of information is creating a certain state of nervousness among professionals themselves and the population.”

News.title: Fury as Greens’ Polanski wrongly claims knife-wielding Golders Green suspect ‘was handcuffed’ when cops kicked his head
News.content:
'IT'S UNTRUE!' Fury as Greens’ Polanski wrongly claims knife-wielding Golders Green suspect ‘was handcuffed’ when cops kicked his head

ZACK Polanski sparked fresh outrage today after wrongly claiming the Golders Green terror suspect had been “handcuffed” as armed cops wrestled him to the ground.

The Green Party boss made the claim during an interview on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme as he tried to defend his previous criticism of the police response.





Mr Polanski said: “Two things can be true at the same time: officers are incredibly brave when they run towards scenes of crimes that most people, including myself, will want to run away from.

“At the same time, I think it is accurate, and that I was also traumatised by seeing someone handcuffed and repeatedly kicked in the head.”

But footage of the arrest appears to show the suspect’s hands were free while he was still clutching a knife.

The suspect had moments earlier allegedly launched a stabbing rampage in Golders Green.



Two Jewish men were seriously injured in the attack.

The incident was later declared terror-related by the Met Police and a suspect was subsequently charged with attempted murder.



The footage showed armed officers wrestling the suspect to the ground outside a kosher restaurant as bystanders watched on.

Mr Polanski first sparked outrage after reposting a social media clip accusing police of using excessive force during the arrest.

He later apologised for sharing the post.

But he then reignited the row by insisting police “should not be above scrutiny” and saying he remained concerned about whether the force used had been proportionate.

His comments triggered a furious backlash from ministers, police supporters and Jewish groups.



Today’s fresh intervention immediately reopened the row.

Labour MP David Taylor accused the Green leader of “spreading fake news” about officers who “stopped a terrorist in his tracks”.

Mr Taylor said: “Zack Polanski just can’t help himself.

“Instead of properly apologising for his attacks on the brave police officers who stopped a terrorist in his tracks, he’s spreading fake news about what actually happened. It’s about time he set the record straight.

“I do agree with him on one thing though – that we do justice in court. So I’m sure he’ll agree that the conviction of Palestine Action activists yesterday was very welcome.”



Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp branded the Greens “dangerous and deluded” and said the officers involved “deserve our full support”.

He said: “The attacker was still holding a knife and might even have had a bomb. The use of substantial force was completely justified.”

Mr Philp also blasted Mr Polanski’s “armchair policing views”, saying he “has no idea” about the danger officers faced during the fast-moving incident.

The latest row comes after polling by More in Common showed Mr Polanski’s approval ratings plunging by 14 points in a single week following his original intervention over the terror attack.

It also comes as the number of antisemitic hate crimes recorded last month by the Metropolitan Police in London was the highest in two years.



Some 140 offences were logged across the capital in April, up from 98 in March and 67 in February, according to new data published by the force.

The borough of Barnet saw the highest number, accounting for 51 of the 140, or 36 per cent.

Barnet includes the districts of Golders Green, Hendon and Finchley, all of which have large Jewish populations, where a string of apparent antisemitic attacks took place last month.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Attempted arson attacks were carried out at Finchley Reform Synagogue on April 15, at the building of a former Jewish charity in Hendon on April 18, and at a memorial wall in Golders Green on April 28.

News.title: Man creeped out after finding previous owner's hidden stash during renovation
News.content:
Man creeped out after finding previous owner's hidden stash during renovation

A homeowner was left baffled when he uncovered a 15-year-old secret hidden in the crawl space of his new home left behind by the previous owner during a home renovation project

View Image He was creeped out by the discovery (stock image) (Image: Susumu Yoshioka via Getty Images)

When settling into a new property, most homeowners are eager to make it their own. However, one man received rather more than he anticipated when he began exploring his new home as part of renovation works. On Reddit, the homeowner described how he uncovered a former resident's secret hidden away in the crawl space.

‌



He wrote: "This 15-year-old stash of canned food I found in my crawl space from the house's previous owner." Accompanying his post was a photograph of the find, revealing shelves stocked with survival-style provisions including cooking oil, pasta, tinned peaches, tomatoes, peas, and jars of pickled goods.

‌



He added: "Bought the house a year ago. The inspector noted there was a stash of bins, canned food, and water in the crawl space. We asked the owner to remove it. He apparently did, but not all of it.

‌



"This section of the crawl space is isolated from the rest and hard to access due to the foundation. Finally made it over there this weekend and this is what I found, plus a dozen Home Depot bins labelled rice, ramen, MREs, potatoes, etc.

"There are gallon jugs of water with expiration dates in late 2008. This tracks with what we heard that the previous owner got really into prepping after Obama was elected.

‌



"Supposedly there are things buried in our backyard as well." The surprising find quickly generated responses online, with numerous users entertained by the combination of emergency preparedness and chaotic time capsule.

One person said: "A few of those cans look brand new, while the rest are fully post-apocalyptic."

Another user recounted a comparable discovery, saying: "We found a space like this under my grandfather's kitchen during a renovation under the floor.

‌



"He had stored about 30 gallons of leaded gasoline right under the stove floorboards. He had that same spinach in cans from the 60s."

A third commented: "Upside is nearly two cases of free mason jars. Downside is literally everything else."

Others contemplated their own approaches to food storage and household security.

Article continues below

One user explained: "My wife and I both grew up pretty poor (food insecure poor).

"As we've moved through our adult lives, we find that a full pantry is one of those things we both just... appreciate. We grocery shop every week, but mostly just perishables."

They continued: "We could generally go about a month without major grocery shopping if we really needed to. We'd notice it after about a week, but with dry goods like flour and rice we keep on hand, we could make it a long time."

News.title: New 'contingency' plan to 'conserve jet fuel' could mean changes to 2026 flights
News.content:
New 'contingency' plan to 'conserve jet fuel' could mean changes to 2026 flights

The UK Government has relaxed a rule for airlines which could see some summer flights dropped to save jet fuel

View 2 Images Flight services could be consolidated at no penalty to airlines (Image: Jackyenjoyphotography via Getty Images)

Travellers could find their UK flights rescheduled as the Government relaxes a particular rule that airlines rarely risk breaking. Holiday-makers should be aware that their plans may be changed to avoid journeys that would result in "wasted fuel".

‌



Transport Department officials say airlines may consider scrapping certain services following the introduction of a temporary rule change that allows carriers to merge flights and combine passengers. The idea is meant to cut the total number of aircraft departing, aiming to preserve jet fuel and provide holidaymakers with reassurance that trips won't be cancelled altogether.

‌



Rather than axing flights at short notice, the idea is to "reduce wasted fuel from flying near-empty planes". To maximise the use of airport departures, airlines would reassess their schedules and could transfer passengers from under-booked services that haven't sold a decent proportion of seats onto similar flights.

‌



The Government claims these "contingency preparations" are meant to "give families greater confidence when travelling this summer". While airlines have always been able to cancel and rebook flights, doing so typically came with a future risk to their business, reports the Express.

Addressing the update, Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander said: "Since the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, the government has been monitoring jet fuel supplies daily and working with airlines, airports and fuel suppliers to stay ahead of any problems. There are no immediate supply issues, but we're preparing now to give families long-term certainty and avoid unnecessary disruption at the departure gate this summer.

View 2 Images Flights could be axed to avoid 'wasted' jet fuel on 'near-empty planes' (Image: Torsten Asmus via Getty Images)

‌



"This legislation will give airlines the tools to adjust flights in good time if they need to, which helps protect passengers and businesses. We will do everything we can to insulate our country from the impact of the situation in the Middle East."

The measures being considered by the government go further by enabling airlines to plan ahead and act on the most reliable information available on fuel supply or the wider ramifications of the Middle East conflict, rather than waiting for shortages to materialise. The government remains engaged in planning for various contingencies to boost flexibility around jet fuel supply, and domestic jet fuel production has risen. The UK sources jet fuel from multiple countries that don't rely on the Strait, including the United States.

Explaining how flight consolidation works, TikTok user and travel specialist Kate Donnelly (@Thedonnellyedit) said: "If an airline has four flights operating to the same destination across a day, they might look at them and see two are half empty, so they might combine them and cancel one of those flights altogether. This would mean they are obviously saving on the amount of jet fuel they are using and overall cost."

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

If a flight experiences a significant delay, passengers are entitled to care and assistance, including food, drink and overnight accommodation where necessary. Generally, delays that warrant this include at least two hours for short-haul, three hours for medium-haul and four hours for long-haul.

Rob Bishton, chief executive of the UK Civil Aviation Authority, said: "Passengers in the UK are well protected by some of the strongest rights in the world, offering reassurance if disruption does occur. Airlines have a duty to look after their passengers when they face disruption, and should offer a choice between a refund or alternative travel arrangements, including with another airline, if a flight is cancelled.

Article continues below

"Relaxing the rules around slots at airports will allow airlines more flexibility and so we expect them to give passengers as much notice as possible of cancellations during this period."

If the airline cancels your flight, you're legally entitled to a choice between being rerouted or receiving a refund. Find out more about your rights following a flight cancellation here.

News.title: Killer brutally murdered chef before using his bank card for booze and scratchcards
News.content:
Killer brutally murdered chef before using his bank card for booze and scratchcards

Adam Rowson, 26, was found guilty of murdering 45-year-old chef Alexis De Naray who was found dead in an abandoned building near the Shelton water tower in Shrewsbury

View 2 Images Adam Rowson was found guilty of murder (Image: West Mercia Police)

A man who brutally killed a head chef and used his bankcard to buy alcohol and scratchcards has been jailed.

‌



Adam Rowson, 26, was found guilty of murdering Alexis De Naray on April 8 following a 12-day trial and has been sentenced today at Stafford Crown Court over his “fierce, sustained and relentless” attack.

‌



Jailing him for life with a minimum term of 16 years, Judge Avik Mukherjee said Rowson, of no fixed abode, had believed he had killed Mr De Naray when he “callously” used his card and “freely spent his money on anything that pleased you” until he was stopped by the bank.

‌



The defendant, who wore glasses and a blue T-shirt with a collar in the dock, showed no emotion and nodded his head as the judge handed down his sentence.

View 2 Images Alexis De Naray had worked in high-end kitchens (Image: LinkedIn)

The court heard Rowson and Mr De Naray, 45, had met at the Royal Shrewsbury Hospital in the early hours of June 24 last year and within a short period of time, the defendant had offered the victim, who was also an alcoholic, a place to stay for one night.

‌



Judge Mukherjee said: “By the time you left him in the disused garage, probably on the 25th June, he had been so severely beaten by you he was dying or dead.

“You left him in that physical state. Rather than calling for help, you left him to die. You covered his body… because you knew what you had done to him.”

Rowson left Mr De Naray, who studied at Leiths School of Food and Wine and had previously worked at Claridge’s, with a traumatic brain injury and 20 rib fractures, three of which occurred after his death, and multiple injuries to his head, torso and upper limbs.

‌



The nature of his injuries are usually associated with stamping or kicks or strikes with objects, and a post-mortem examination found Mr De Naray had defensive injuries to his back consistent with him being in a foetal position to protect himself.

In a victim impact statement read out by prosecution counsel Sally Howes KC, Alexandros De Naray said his older brother was “one of the most caring and loving people I have ever known”.

He said: “He was my best friend I loved him more than I could ever explain… I think every day how I can never see him again and one of the people I loved most in the world has been taken away from me in such a horrible way.

‌



“I can only hope he felt no pain in his last moments and he is now at peace. I just hope everyone remembers he was a kind and loving person who meant so much to us and will always been in our memories every day.”

His father Constantine De Naray said his son was “funny, kind, thoughtful, generous and a loving son”. He said: “My wonderful boy did not deserve to lose his life… He was a dear son who we will forever miss.

“He was a very talented chef who worked in London until he became unwell and moved to Shrewsbury to be close to family. He was gradually getting better when he sadly lost his life. No parent should have to bury a child, more especially in these horrendous circumstances.”

‌



In his sentencing remarks, Judge Mukherjee said: “It is clear the person they knew and loved so very dearly was warm, kind-hearted, compassionate and courageous. He never gave up on people. He was a damaged and vulnerable person who was struggling with alcoholism up until his passing.”

He told Rowson: “He was a survivor and he survived up until he had the misfortune of meeting you.” The judge said in his view, Rowson had been fully aware he had killed Mr De Naray in his brutal assault but did not call the emergency services for days, before he pretended he had found the body.

He also threw away a T-shirt he had been wearing, which the judge said showed how “forensically astute your thinking was at the time”. Rowson allegedly told a friend: “Have you heard about the situation, it got bad bro, I don’t even want to go home because I think I killed someone.”

Article continues below

The judge added: “You lied to the emergency services, you lied to police at the scene. Only you know the full detail of what you did. I’m sure you have not told the truth at any stage about the assault on Alexis.”

Defending, Michelle Heeley KC said Rowson was sorry and that alcohol and drugs had contributed “significantly” to what he had done. She said: “Through me he would like to apologise… he recognises the pain he has caused the family.

“He is still a relatively young man, 26 now and not particularly mature. While in custody he has found a job… he is trying to pay his debt in some minor way. The structure has benefitted him. He is clean now of drink and drugs. He can say no more other than he is sorry and accepts the punishment of the court.”

News.title: Andes virus explainer - symptoms, how it's spread, treatment and where it's endemic
News.content:
Andes virus explainer - symptoms, how it's spread, treatment and where it's endemic

Passengers and crew on the luxury MV Hondius have been forced to stay on board following a suspected hantavirus outbreak on the cruise - officials have identified which strain has infected some people on the vessel

View 5 Images An ambulance boat approaching the MV Hondius (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

A suspected hantavirus outbreak has broken out on a cruise ship as three passengers from the vessel have died - officials have identified the specific strain.

‌



Hantavirus is a rare disease that can sometimes be spread from rodents to humans but the World Health Organisation said it could have spread among "really close contacts". Around 150 people remain stuck on the luxury liner MV Hondius as it sits off the coast of West Africa. Three passengers, including an elderly married couple, on the luxury Dutch liner have died, with one so far testing positive for hantavirus.

‌



Other cases include a critically ill passenger, who is being treated in a hospital in Johannesburg, and three other people have reported mild symptoms.

‌



Hantavirus outbreak cruise ship rescue plan being drawn up for Brits stranded on MV Hondius READ MORE :

View 5 Images Health workers on the MV Hondius on May 4 (Image: AP)

South Africa's health ministry revealed that the two confirmed cases are linked to the Andes strain of hantavirus. Health officials have shared information and guidance on the rare but potentially fatal disease.

This virus can lead to hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) which is a complication that impacts the heart and lungs, which has a high mortality rate, according to the NHS. Only certain type of hantavirus can lead to HCPS and the Andes strain is one of them.

‌



Symptoms

Health officials revealed the initial signs of the Andes virus can present with flu-like symptoms. This could include a fever, chills, muscle pain and sometimes gastrointestinal symptoms.

Respiratory symptoms tend to be absent at the start but these symptoms can show as the illness gets worse. For example, infected people could experience a dry cough which come from leakage from the capillaries into the lungs.

View 5 Images Map of the journey the hantavirus cruise has been on (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



At this stage, other signs could include worse flu-like symptoms and abdominal pain, according to the NHS. Severe complications could arise as the illness progresses for example: respiratory failure, shock and haemorrhage.

Health officials also added that symptoms usually do not show immediately and usually start one to eight weeks later, according to the World Health Organisation. The illness typically develops two to four weeks after someone has been exposed to the Andes virus.

How is Andes virus spread?

Hantavirus can spread from animals to humans when people come into contact with infected rodents and their droppings, saliva or urine. This can include breathing in particles from infected droppings and touching infected parts with hands. It can also be contracted through rodent bites but this is very unlikely. Infected rodents do not show signs of the disease.

‌



Officials added that the Andes variant is spread between humans through "close contact" with an infected person, adding that it can often happen between families.

View 5 Images People in hazmat suits visiting the MV Hondius (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Treatment

There is no proven specific treatment or vaccine for hantavirus or the Andes strain. Care for the infected is supportive and doctors will help treat respiratory, cardiac and kidney complications. The WHO added that diagnosing the virus early makes a big difference in managing the disease.

‌



Where is the Andes virus present?

The Andes variant of hantavirus comes from infected rodents in South America, according to the NHS. The countries where the virus has been reported in the past include Argentina and Chile.

View 5 Images Inside the luxury MV Hondius vessel (Image: AP)

The WHO revealed the 70-year-old man his 69-year-old wife who died had travelled through South America, including Argentina, before they boarded the vessel.

Article continues below

The MV Hondius had been waiting off the coast of Cape Verde, after the island country refused to allow the cruise to dock. The ship had started heading towards the Canary Islands but the leader of the Spanish island group, on Wednesday morning, said he is refusing to allow the vessel to dock.

WHO director general Tedros Ghebreyesus said three patients have been evacuated from the liner and are being taken to the Netherlands for medical care.

News.title: Derby school in emergency lockdown as armed police race to the scene

Derby school in emergency lockdown as armed police race to the scene

Police were called to reports of a man potentially having a weapon outside Derby Cathedral School just as pupils were due to leave for the day

View Image Armed officers were deployed to the secondary school before a man was arrested (Image: Derby Cathedral School)

A secondary school was plunged into lockdown with pupils kept inside and armed police racing to the scene.

‌



Derbyshire Police said officers were called to reports of a man potentially having a weapon outside Derby Cathedral School just before 3pm on Tuesday - when pupils were due to leave school for the day.

‌



Armed officers were deployed before a man was located and arrested on suspicion of common assault, coercive and controlling behaviour and false imprisonment, the force said.

‌



"We were called to reports of a man potentially having a weapon in Great Northern Road, Derby, just before 3pm," a spokesperson said. "No weapon had been seen, and nobody was threatened or injured.

"Armed officers were deployed to the scene, and a man was located and arrested." Police said no weapon was found and there was no risk to the public, reports Derbyshire Live.

Article continues below

The statement added: "Pupils from a nearby school were briefly held inside while officers ensured the safe arrest of the man, and then they were able to leave the school.

"Following inquiries, the incident is understood to be a domestic incident. The man, who is in his 30s and from Derby, was arrested on suspicion of common assault, coercive and controlling behaviour and false imprisonment. He remains in police custody."

News.title: The Traitors star and Booker winners join UK book festival's massive 2026 line up
News.content:
The Traitors star and Booker winners join UK book festival's massive 2026 line up

The Edinburgh International Book Festival has unveiled its star-studded Front List for 2026, featuring Douglas Stuart and Diana Gabaldon in a series of major conversations at McEwan Hall.

View 2 Images Booker prize winning author Douglas Stuart leads the star-studded Front List

The Edinburgh International Book Festival has today announced The Front List, its series of headline events at McEwan Hall during this year’s Festival (15–30 August), bringing together some of the most significant writers, historians, journalists and cultural thinkers working today.

‌



Taking place in the Festival’s largest venue, and presented in partnership with Underbelly, The Front List offers audiences rare opportunities to hear from internationally celebrated voices whose work helps shape how contemporary culture, politics, history and society are understood.

‌



From Booker Prize winning novelists and globally bestselling storytellers to frontline correspondents, historians and public intellectuals, the series places big ideas and major conversations at the heart of the 2026 Festival.

‌



View 2 Images The Traitors star David Olusoga also appears amid a new season of A House Through Time

6 unmissable books coming out in May from Kathryn Stockett and Douglas Stuart READ MORE :

Pointless star and author Richard Osman receives OBE from Princess Royal at Windsor Castle READ MORE :

The programme spans fiction, media, history, politics and performance. It opens with a timely examination of the future of the internet, as Wikipedia founder Jimmy Wales and Cory Doctorow consider who now holds power online and whether the early days of altruism and optimism about the internet are gone for good.

Elsewhere, audiences can enjoy a rare appearance from Diana Gabaldon, marking thirty-five years since the publication of Outlander, as she reflects on one of the most successful literary franchises of recent decades, credited - alongside its screen adaptations - with transforming both Scotland’s tourism and its film and television industry.

‌



World-leading fiction sits at the heart of the series, featuring an array of celebrated authors. Colson Whitehead, the Pulitzer Prize-winning novelist behind The Underground Railroad, joins journalist and broadcaster Samira Ahmed. Douglas Stuart, the Booker Prize-winning writer of Shuggie Bain, will appear in conversation with poet, novelist and former Makar Jackie Kay.

The line-up also includes Booker Prize winner Kiran Desai and Ann Patchett, the Pulitzer Prize and PEN/Faulkner-winning novelist. They are joined by Elif Shafak, the internationally bestselling writer and global public intellectual. Together, these writers explore memory, migration, identity, belonging, race and the moral responsibilities of storytelling.

Want to hear the latest books news and reviews from The Mirror's resident bookworm? Follow Aimée Walsh on Tiktok and Instagram

‌



The Front List also places contemporary journalism at the centre of the programme. Lyse Doucet, the BBC’s Chief International Correspondent, reflects on decades reporting from conflict zones and geopolitical fault lines.

History and public memory are explored in depth during the series. David Olusoga also appears amid a new season of A House Through Time. Fresh from his role unpacking power, loyalty and betrayal on The Traitors, he considers empire, memory and Britain’s contested past.

‌



Performance, warmth and joy also run through The Front List. Kae Tempest, the multi-award-winning poet, novelist and musician reflects on language, identity and creativity across a body of work spanning poetry, fiction and performance.

Charlie Mackesy, creator of the global phenomenon The Boy, the Mole, the Fox and the Horse – winner of the Waterstones Book of the Year and adapted into an Academy Award winning animated film – appears in a family friendly event centred on kindness, vulnerability and connection.

At a moment when public debate can often feel polarised or diminished, The Front List reflects the Festival’s belief in the value of open, inspiring and nuanced conversation. Bringing together readers and audiences with some of the most compelling voices of our time, the series underscores the Edinburgh International Book Festival’s position as one of the world’s leading forums for literature, ideas and public exchange.

News.title: 'I work in travel - it's safer to book package holidays right now'
News.content:
'I work in travel - it's safer to book package holidays right now'

A travel specialist has suggested booking package holidays in case of cancellations

View 2 Images Holidaymakers don't want to get caught out (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

Holidaymakers have been told they could enjoy more consumer protection if they book a package holiday, according to a travel specialist. Amid reports of airlines trying to conserve jet fuel following the Middle East conflict, many travellers are asking what would happen if their flights are cancelled this summer.

‌



While Gov.uk says there are no immediate jet fuel supply issues and preparations are being made to avoid disruption, many people are still planning ahead so they know what might happen in a worst-case scenario. According to travel professionals, it could depend on how you made your booking.

‌



Rob Brooks, a travel specialist and influencer with the travel company, On The Beach, claims: "Package holidays are safer right now." He argues: "If you book flights and hotels separately, you’re on your own when things go wrong.

‌



"But with a package holiday, everything’s protected - so if your flight’s cancelled, you’re covered. I work in travel, and this is exactly why more people choose package holidays." Rob shared his claim on TikTok under the username @Robonthebeach. He is known for posting budget-friendly travel advice, hotel reviews, and holiday tips to his 139k followers.

In his post, Rob reiterated advice Martin Lewis shared - that people who book flights and hotels separately could risk losing money if their transport arrangements go wrong. In a video posted on his official TikTok, the MoneySavingExpert founder has previously told viewers that how you book can make a big difference to your consumer rights.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



When Martin was asked if you definitely receive your money back for a hotel booking when flights are cancelled, he said: "No, no – and this is what I think people need to be very aware of. If you have booked a package holiday, where you booked everything in one, and under the Package Holiday Regulations and rules and protections, generally, if your flight went, you will get everything back.

"So actually, at the moment, package holidays give you a certain level of extra surety that you wouldn't get if you did a DIY booking – where you book your hotel and flight separately."

However, Martin said you might not be protected if you completed a DIY booking. "The issue is you can't get there. Your hotel is still there. It's not faulty. It's not cancelling. So you don't get those consumer rights," he explained.

‌



View 2 Images Many people are booking holidays ahead of summer (stock photo) (Image: Getty)

As a result, holidaymakers may prefer to book with package providers. Responding to Martin's advice, Rob told his followers: "I've actually been wanting to make this video for a while now, but to be honest I didn't want to come across as biased because I actually work for a package holiday company. But now the king of saving money has spoken about it, I can talk about it properly."

He continued: "The bottom line is this, if you book your flight and your hotel separately, they don't work together. So if your flight gets cancelled, your hotel's not really done anything wrong. It's still there, it's still booked, and most of the time, unfortunately, you don't get your money back, and I think a lot of people don't realise that. However, package holidays are completely different."

‌



Rob claims: "When you book with a package holiday company, like On the Beach, LoveHolidays, Jet2 Holidays, or TUI, everything gets booked together. So if your flight does get cancelled, it's not just your problem anymore; it's the holiday company's problem to fix for you.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"That usually means one of two things: either you find another flight that's suitable, or they have to refund the whole thing. About 99% of flights are still going ahead as planned. So this is just small pockets of disruption, but when you are in that 1%, that's when this really, really matters."

‌



The Mirror contacted several travel companies in response to the video. For customers booking with On the Beach, the package holiday company has committed to same-day processing of refunds for any cancelled flights. Under the scheme, On the Beach said that if your flight is cancelled, it will find you an alternative flight or give you a full refund on your entire holiday, processing it on the same day.

Caspar Nelson, holiday expert at On the Beach, said: "Holidaymakers deserve certainty, especially when disruption strikes. We’re proud to be the first package holiday provider to commit to same-day refund processing for cancelled flights, giving customers the confidence to book knowing we’ve got their back when it matters most.

"If the worst happens and a flight is cancelled, we’ll move quickly to either find a new route or return every penny of their holiday money that same day, so they can get a new break booked, make alternative plans fast, and get back to looking forward to their summer instead of worrying about it."

Article continues below

A loveholidays spokesperson said: "There are still plenty of affordable getaways available this summer and booking a package holiday gives consumers built-in protection so they can travel with confidence. In the unlikely event of disruption prior to travel, such as a cancelled flight where no suitable alternative is available, customers are entitled to a full refund of their holiday under the Package Travel Regulations – added protection you wouldn’t get by booking your flight and hotel separately. All of our package holidays are also protected by the ‘gold standard’ ATOL scheme, alongside our own secure trust account, so holidaymakers can relax knowing their holiday is in safe hands from start to finish."

Ahead of summer, some people may still prefer DIY bookings. In these cases, holidaymakers may wish to consider hotels with free or limited cancellation. It's also advised to check your travel insurance, as your policy may not cover your hotel if your flight is cancelled.

The Mirror has contacted Jet2 Holidays and TUI for comment.

News.title: Universal Credit, PIP and Carer's Allowance change in force – BBC expert says check your account
News.content:
Universal Credit, PIP and Carer's Allowance change in force – BBC expert says check your account

A BBC personal finance expert has urged people claiming Universal Credit, PIP and Carer's Allowance to check their accounts after an increase came into force

View Image BBC Morning Live personal finance expert Laura Pomfret explained recent benefits changes (Image: BBC)

A BBC finance expert has urged those claiming Universal Credit, Personal Independence Payments and Carer's Allowance to check their accounts following a significant change in May. Personal finance specialist Laura Pomfret appeared on BBC Morning Live alongside hosts Rav Wilding and Holly Hamilton, revealing that benefits claimants have received a welcome boost — but need to confirm the increase has actually landed in their accounts.

‌



She pointed out that those who typically receive payments on Monday April 4 should have been paid the preceding Friday due to the bank holiday, with payments rising by 3.8%. Ms Pomfret explained: "So, we've had we've had awful April, which we kept referring to, and but we did see a positive thing in April, which is the increase in benefits, and we've had the first month of that now.

‌



"So they've gone up this year by this tax year. So, that's universal credit, personal independent payment, carers allowance, all gone up. So, if you are someone on benefits, you should have got paid on Friday because it's a bank holiday today and so check that you had that higher amount. That's one thing that's really important that you will have seen that increase because we're talking about food prices, we're talking about things going up. Make sure that you've got that increase."

‌



Universal Credit change

Person’s situation // Standard amount before 6 April 2026 // Standard amount from 6 April 2026

Single and under 25 // £316.98 a month // £338.58 a month

‌



Single and 25 or over // £400.14 a month // £424.90 a month

Living with a partner and both under 25 // £497.55 a month // £528.34 a month

Living with a partner and one or both over 25 // £628.10 a month //£666.97 a month

‌



Personal Independence Payment (PIP) rates

The government has confirmed that Personal Independence Payment (PIP) rates increased by 3.8% from April 2026

The new rates apply from 6 April 2026.

Daily Living

‌



Standard rate: £76.70 per week (up from £73.90). £306.80 per month.

Enhanced rate: £114.60 per week (up from £110.40). £458.40 per month.

Mobility

Standard rate: £30.30 per week (up from £29.20). £121.20 per month.

Enhanced rate: £80 per week (up from £77.05). £320 per month.

‌



Carer's Allowance

From April 6, 2026, the Carer’s Allowance weekly rate increases to £86.45 (up £3.15). To maintain eligibility, the earnings threshold rises to £204 per week. Other changes include increased payments for the Carer Element of Universal Credit to £209.34 monthly and the Carer Addition for Pension Credit to £48.15 weekly.

From 6 April 2026, the weekly Carer's Allowance rate climbs to £86.45 (an increase of £3.15). To remain eligible, the earnings limit rises to £204 per week. Additional changes include the Carer Element of Universal Credit increasing to £209.34 monthly and the Carer Addition for Pension Credit rising to £48.15 weekly.

Ms Pomfret also highlighted another change 'affecting some parents'. She said: "We've got a headline, the DWP universal credit change this month that parents need to know. This is removing the restriction on the two-child benefit cap that you may have seen and talked about a lot in the press.

Article continues below

"This is now you're going to be able to receive a payment for all the children that you have an entitlement to receive this for. It applies to both new and existing parents both of which will benefit for this. So we've got the £333 all the threes for a month for a first child born before April 6 2017 and then £287.92 a month for each additional child.

"And over a year that's worth more than £3,400 per child. So we you weren't getting this. This is a big increase for families at a time when you need it the most. So, it's just like a nice reminder. Make sure we check that we've got what we're entitled to. This is the first month that you should have received it. And because with those food prices, we're going to need it "

News.title: Spencer Matthews says he’s found new purpose and health through endurance challenges
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Once a fixture of reality television, Spencer Matthews has undergone a profound transformation, shedding his former persona to embrace fatherhood, entrepreneurship, and the demanding world of endurance athletics. The 37-year-old, known for his appearances on Made In Chelsea, now speaks of a life driven by purpose, a stark contrast to periods where he felt he "lacked purpose".

"I’ve gone through years and years of not caring about anything and going out all the time," Matthews reflects, having recently completed the London Marathon in an impressive three hours and four seconds, in collaboration with The Turmeric Co. He admits to having "long periods in my life where I’ve felt that I’ve really lacked purpose. I’ve not really enjoyed the things I’m doing and just been a half version of myself."

For Matthews, who also hosts the podcast Untapped where he interviews athletes, this shift towards a more fulfilling existence began just a few years ago. "I think for anyone ambitious, you want to try to live up to what you can be – and that only really started for me a few years ago." He attributes this change in mindset to a renewed focus on fitness and wellbeing.

"To me, my physical and mental health is probably the most important part of my life plan," he asserts. "If you’re not well and healthy and living a full life, everything you’re striving for feels a little bit more pointless."

open image in gallery ( The Turmeric Co/Tom Harrison Photography )

This commitment has manifested in a series of gruelling endurance challenges. In 2024, Matthews ran 30 marathons in 30 days across the Jordanian desert, earning him a Guinness World Record for "the most consecutive marathons run on sand". He followed this by tackling seven triathlons on seven continents in 21 days in 2025, a feat dubbed ‘Project Se7en’, which secured him two additional world records.

"Endurance challenges are great goals to have," he explains. "I operate better when I have goals to chase."

Matthews, who also founded the non-alcoholic spirits brand CleanCo in 2019, finds that maintaining focus is crucial for his sense of direction. "Boredom is a bit of a trigger of mine," he reveals. "But now, I haven’t felt bored in a very long time." He adds, "For me, unless there’s something to target, it’s quite easy to bend the rules on exercise. I find having one massive goal a year fun to work towards."

Beyond personal achievement, a sense of purpose, often linked to charitable causes, underpins his efforts. "I feel very privileged to be able to do some of the events that I’ve done," he says, noting that "being able to travel the world and raise money has also felt quite purposeful to me." His Project Se7en challenge, for instance, supported James’ Place, a charity dedicated to preventing male suicide in the UK.

open image in gallery Matthews visited Mount Everest in search of his lost brother for the 2023 documentary ‘Finding Michael’ ( Disney+/PA )

He recalls a particularly challenging moment during an Ironman triathlon in Cape Town, South Africa, which involves a 2.4-mile swim, 112-mile bike ride, and a 26.2-mile marathon run. "I had about 15 minutes in the water where I was really struggling and felt quite frightened," he recounts.

"But I had to stop and think: I’m in Cape Town doing an Ironman – this is something special." This moment of reflection brought a deeper perspective. "I myself don’t have any experience with suicidal thoughts, but I thought, imagine waking up and not wanting to be here anymore. All of sudden it rationalises where you are and I found that moment quite helpful to understand that what I was doing could potentially help some of these men who are not in a good headspace."

For anyone considering their own challenges, Matthews offers practical advice: "It sounds silly, but really making an effort to try and enjoy training and races helps." He acknowledges the physical toll: "When you start to feel crushed, tired, full of lactic acid, slow and heavy, that becomes a pretty serious reality. If that’s all you’re thinking about, it’s pretty difficult. So try and enjoy it."

He also emphasises the temporary nature of discomfort during exercise. "Any pain you’re feeling is going to come to an end," he assures. "You will regret giving up almost immediately. Just strap in for the pain, try and enjoy it and it’s a lesson that you’ll remember. You’ll remember that pain and you could perhaps use it in other ways."

open image in gallery Spencer Matthews and his wife Vogue Williams ( PA )

However, Matthews cautions against overtraining, suggesting that going "too hard all the time" can lead to "consequences to pay". With research from The Turmeric Co indicating that 47 per cent of people use pain relief just to continue exercising, he stresses the equal importance of recovery. "We’re human beings. We’re not machines. I focus on easy wins that exist to give myself an edge so I can train and not get injured," he explains. "Turmeric is a great example of a scientifically proven concept that is affordable and really easy to use. It’s one shot in the morning, full of antioxidants and anti-inflammatory."

Away from his rigorous training schedule, Matthews, who is expecting his fourth child with wife Vogue Williams, prioritises maintaining balance at home. "I spend time with my kids and my wife. I try not to sacrifice the things that matter," he says. "I work very hard and fortunately so does my wife. We spend our evenings together – we’re usually in bed early and our evenings are about winding down together."

Reflecting on his past lifestyle, the contrast is clear. "I’ve gone through years of not caring and going out all the time – I know which I prefer," he states. "If you put in the time and consistency, good things happen. It sounds obvious, but it took me a long time to realise that." Matthews collaborated with The Turmeric Co. to highlight their offer of free joint support turmeric shots to those who ran a marathon this April.

Were they on a break? It’s the age-old question that’s plagued Friends viewers for almost 30 years – and now Lisa Kudrow has given her blunt verdict.

Kudrow, who played Phoebe Buffay in the long-running Nineties sitcom, was asked about the plot line in which Ross Gellar (David Schwimmer) slept with another woman while going through a rough patch with girlfriend Rachel Green (Jennifer Aniston).

Ross later makes it clear he believed he and Rachel had broken up at the time of his encounter with Chloe. Rachel, however, disagrees and considers that Ross’s behaviour amounts to cheating.

open image in gallery Were Ross and Rachel on a break? ‘Friends’ fans have debated this since the 1990s ( NBC )

Throughout the show, the sentence “we were on a break” is uttered several more times, becoming one of the sitcom’s most memorable one-liners.

Whether or not he actually was is the source of intense debate, and Kudrow has now waded in, stating: “It’s beyond break or not. He was a bad boyfriend.”

Speaking on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, Kudrow admitted she was afraid to discuss the contentious topic, but when the audience applauded, she said in relief: “Oh, you agree! Oh, I feel better. Thank you. Thank you for this. Thank you, all of you.”

Kudrow continued: “She shouldn’t have gotten back with him because he was horrible.

“To me, it’s like, I don’t care if he slept with three other women or no other women. You had a crisis at work, so you weren’t available for a few nights, and he flipped out.”

open image in gallery Lisa Kudrow waded into the Ross and Rachel debate on ‘The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon’ ( YouTube )

When asked if Schwimmer, who previously defended Ross’s actions, shared this view, Kudrow said: “He knows now.”

Kudrow recently opened up about the “tense” scrutiny faced by Friends’ female cast members, also including Courteney Cox (Monica), due to the mostly male writers’ room.

More than 20 years on from Friends’ finale, Kudrow, who currently stars in HBO sitcom The Comeback, told The Times there was “mean stuff going on behind the scenes”.

“Don’t forget we were recording in front of a live audience of 400, and if you messed up one of these writers’ lines or it didn’t get the perfect response, they could be like, ‘Can’t the bitch f***ing read? She’s not even trying. She f***ed up my line’,” Kudrow said.

“And we know that back in the room, the guys would be up late discussing their sexual fantasies about Jennifer and Courteney. It was intense.”

She added that while it “could be brutal”, the writers were up all night writing on the sitcom. “These guys – and it was mostly men in there – were sitting up until 3am trying to write the show, so my attitude was, ‘Say what you like about me behind my back because then it doesn’t matter’.”

David Haye has revealed he plans to sue ITV for allegedly editing I’m a Celebrity: South Africa to make him look bad – claiming it will be for “way more” than £10m.

The former WBA heavyweight world champion boxer is entering the ring with the channel in his “biggest battle” yet amid claims that the series, in which he made a series of controversial comments, was “heavily directed” and “manipulated” to cause “irreparable damage” to his brand.

On Instagram, Haye, 45, said that the experience had a “detrimental effect on him” and has left him “facing negative repercussions”. In the show, which aired last month, Haye faced criticism for saying that “ugly girls” have a personality whereas “super pretty girls are idiots”, while later in the series, his treatment of Adam Thomas in camp left many viewers feeling uncomfortable.

open image in gallery Legal experts predict David Haye is in for a ‘notoriously difficult’ challenge if he brings a defamation case against ITV ( ITV )

Haye addressed reports he was planning to take legal action against the company for £10m, but said this figure will be higher: “I’m hearing this 10 million number banded around. I don’t know where that came from, because the number I’m going to hit him with is way more than that.”

He said he doesn’t like “getting pushed around” or “people taking advantage”, adding that he’s “going to take it as far as it needs to go” and that he was “looking forward” to the legal battle. Haye expressed confidence that a judge would rule in his favour.

“Once the tapes have been viewed, once the evidence has been presented, and once they see what the public sees, they’ll realise that maybe this, this reality TV, might not be that real, maybe manipulated, heavily directed in a certain narrative for a specific reason,” he told his fans. “And I’m looking forward to a judge seeing exactly what went down so they can make their decision.”

However, media law experts have warned that Haye is in for a “notoriously difficult” challenge, telling The Independent that defamation cases based on reality TV show editing are very unlikely to succeed.

Kishan Pattni, a reputation management partner at Freeths LLP, told The Independent: “Claims arising out of reality TV editing are notoriously difficult to win in England. The law does not protect contestants from being shown in an unflattering or hostile light: it protects against false statements of fact that cause serious harm to reputation, as required by the Defamation Act 2013.”

open image in gallery David Haye ruffled feathers during his time in ‘I’m a Celebrity: South Africa’ ( ITV )

“To succeed, Haye would need to establish that I’m A Celebrity: South Africa conveyed a genuinely false and defamatory meaning presented as fact, rather than a matter of impression, narrative or opinion. Only if that hurdle were cleared would the burden shift to ITV for proving the meaning was true.”

It’s also very likely that contestants will have signed contracts which give producers editorial control of “how footage is selected, edited and presented”.

Joseph McCaughley, a reputational management partner at Spencer West LLP, said: “This often restricts their ability to bring claims about how they are portrayed. A claim will only succeed if the programme crosses the threshold into a legal wrong – not simply because it creates a negative impression.”

The Independent has contacted ITV for comment

The Trump administration has declared the offensive against Iran over and paused its ambitious mission to free ships stuck in the Gulf in a dramatic turnaround over a 48-hour period.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, told reporters at the White House late on Tuesday that Operation Epic Fury is “over” and that the military phase of the war had ended.

Mr Rubio said that the conflict’s new phase, dubbed ‘Project Freedom’, was working to save some 23,000 civilians from 87 countries stranded in the Gulf, insisting this was a purely defensive operation.

But in an abrupt pivot, the President said late on Tuesday that the initiative would also be placed on hold “by mutual agreement” to allow for productive talks aimed at ending the war.

The Independent looks at how a chaotic 48 hours unfolded in the White House.

open image in gallery U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio addresses media on Tuesday, his debut filling in for press secretary Karoline Leavitt ( Reuters )

Sunday: Trump reveals Project Freedom

Renewed talk of diplomacy comes just days after Donald Trump unveiled the Project Freedom initiative, framed as a defensive mission to guide foreign ships out of the Strait of Hormuz and safeguard international trade.

The strait is a vital waterway for global supplies of oil, fertiliser and other commodities that has been virtually closed since the US and Israel attacked Iran on 28 February, causing global price rises.

The president said the operation was a “humanitarian effort to rescue ships running low on essentials after more than two months trapped in the Persian Gulf”.

open image in gallery Donald Trump addressed the Iran crisis at the Oval Office on Tuesday ( AFP/Getty )

Monday: US escorts ships through Hormuz

By the end of its first day, on Monday, the US military said it had escorted two ships through the Strait of Hormuz. But Iran also claimed to have fired warning shots at a US ship, commercial ships reported incoming fire, and a key oil port in the UAE was struck by Iran, according to reports.

In a briefing on the war to reporters, Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth tried to frame Monday’s clashes as natural “churn”, while warning that the US still has the capability to reopen the wider conflict if needed.

“The option is always there, and Iran knows that. And that’s why their choices in Project Freedom are important,” he said, casting the mission as a “gift” to the rest of the world while also downplaying the US’s need for the waterway.

Tuesday: Trump pauses Project Freedom

The UAE accused Iran of more missile and drone attacks on Tuesday as the Trump administration tried to play down attacks in the region.

But after a day of careful positioning from his senior officials, Trump wrote on Truth Social that the operation to rescue commercial shipping “will be paused for a short period of time to see whether or not the Agreement can be finalized and signed”.

It was unclear whether any talks with Iran had been formally agreed or scheduled.

open image in gallery Ships and boats in the Strait of Hormuz, Musandam, Oman, May 4 ( Reuters )

Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said during a state visit to China that Iran would only accept a “fair and comprehensive agreement” in negotiations with the US.

“We will do our best to protect our legitimate rights and interests in the negotiations,” he said, following a meeting with China’s top diplomat, Wang Yi.

Iran has until now brushed off US demands as “maximalist” and rejected coming in for talks so long as the US military continues to enforce its punishing blockade on Iranian ports and vessels.

Trump said that the blockade would “remain in full force and effect” while the escort mission is paused.

The administration has been navigating a deadline that passed last week requiring Trump to seek congressional approval to continue the war. Hegesth has argued the “clock stops” with the ceasefire.

Iran’s parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who previously led Tehran through talks with Washington, said the US was endangering shipping through the strait with what Tehran has dubbed “Project Deadlock”.

“We know full well that the continuation of the status quo is intolerable for America, while we have not even begun yet,” Mr Ghalibaf wrote on social media.
